key_highlights: ASX finishes the week higher buoyed by major bank shares despite retail and consumer sector drag.
RBA rate hike expectations build amid persistent inflation pressures, contrasting with the US Fed rate hold.
Coles suffers heavy market sell-off after losing ground to Woolworths in supermarket sector competition.
Housing market downturn deepens with Sydney dwelling values falling 10% and auction markets at multi-year lows.
Domestic gas supply uncertainty and renewable rollout bottlenecks pose energy policy headwinds.

sectors.trend: Banking majors rebound to support index gains despite macro headwinds and rising mortgage stress.
sectors.implications: Near-term dividend support for CBA.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX, and ANZ.AX; upside capped by decelerating credit growth.

sectors.trend: Coles experiences significant valuation hit as Woolworths expands market share; retail spending weakens under RBA rate pressure.
sectors.implications: Favor WOW.AX over COL.AX on market share momentum; maintain cautious stance on discretionary retail (HVN.AX, JBH.AX).

sectors.trend: Active exploration in junior gold, lithium, and silver alongside ongoing volatility in bulk commodity markets.
sectors.implications: Iron ore majors (BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX) face margin moderation; junior explorers see targeted speculative capital flows.

sectors.trend: Domestic gas supply policy friction and delays in renewable transmission and wind infrastructure.
sectors.implications: Supply tighteners benefit upstream gas producers (WDS.AX, STO.AX); utilities (AGL.AX, ORG.AX) navigate transition challenges.

sectors.trend: Steepening price correction across major residential auction markets while commercial assets see selective deals.
sectors.implications: Downside risks for residential developers (MGR.AX, LLC.AX); gaming and hospitality assets remain resilient.

key_themes: Monetary policy divergence between the RBA (tightening bias) and US Federal Reserve (rates on hold)
Intensifying supermarket price competition and consumer margin compression
Accelerating property market deflation and sovereign/state debt overhang
Energy transition delays and heightened regulatory scrutiny on corporate governance

risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight rate-sensitive consumer discretionary and leveraged property; increase allocation to cash and floating-rate debt.
Limit exposure to pure-play residential developers; monitor mortgage loan arrears across major bank holdings.
Diversify energy exposure toward globally contracted LNG producers rather than purely unhedged domestic suppliers.
Avoid speculative pre-IPO floats and unvetted digital platforms; focus on companies with strong balance sheet transparency.

opportunities.recommendation: Long Woolworths vs Short Coles Pair Trade
opportunities.rationale: Woolworths is winning competitive grocery share while Coles contends with market share erosion and margin degradation.
Tightening domestic gas dynamics and ongoing Middle East geopolitical stalemate support energy pricing.

opportunities.recommendation: Selective Small-Cap Gold and Critical Minerals Exposure
opportunities.rationale: Exploration updates in gold and silver offer uncorrelated return potential amidst macroeconomic hedging demand.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge ASX 200 Exposure via Index Puts
defensive_moves.rationale: RBA rate hike expectations and consumer spending deceleration present asymmetric downside risk to broader equities.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce Exposure to Cyclical Retail and Residential Developers
defensive_moves.rationale: Sydney property price falls of 10% and weak auction clearance rates will further depress discretionary household demand.

market_outlook.short_term: The ASX 200 (^AXJO) is positioned for range-bound consolidation over the next 1–3 months. Banking resilience provides support, but impending RBA rate hike risks and weak consumer earnings will cap broader index gains.
market_outlook.long_term: Over a 6–12 month horizon, subdued consumer spending and state debt consolidation will weigh on domestic economic growth. Outperformance will favor cash-generative energy and defensive staples over leveraged cyclicals.
key_catalysts: RBA cash rate decisions and monetary policy statements
Quarterly Australian CPI inflation and labour force data
Federal government domestic gas policy announcements
Australian major bank interim earnings reports and net interest margin updates
watch_list: AUD/USD currency movements around key technical levels
Sydney and Melbourne weekly auction clearance rates and CoreLogic dwelling values
Benchmark iron ore (62% Fe CFR China) and thermal/coking coal spot prices
Australian 3-year and 10-year Commonwealth Government Bond yields
